headline: Claude for Startups now offers a free year of Claude Team
dek: Anthropic adds API credits and widens who can apply (TechCrunch, TechRadar).

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A new version of an old program
body: Anthropic announced an expanded Claude for Startups program during SF Tech Week, an annual tech event in San Francisco. It offers subsidized access to its models for early-stage companies (TechCrunch, TechRadar).
The core offer is a free year of Claude Team, Anthropic's paid plan for groups, with up to five premium seats, plus $1,000 in API credits to build with Claude (TechCrunch, TechRadar).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Who gets in and what they get
s3.body: Companies founded within the last five years, or funded within the last two, can apply directly on the program page (TechCrunch, TechRadar).

points.t: The $1,000 in API credits arrive on approval and expire six months later (TechRadar).
The five Claude Team seats go only to companies that are not already Claude Team customers (TechRadar).
Startups get Claude Marketplace access, a plug-in storefront, and office hours with Anthropic's Applied AI team (TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A race for early customers
body: AI vendors are competing to win customers while they are small, betting that early platform choices tend to stick as a company grows.
Anthropic says AI's benefits reach most people through companies that build on its models, not through the models alone, which is why it works closely with founders (TechCrunch).

stat.cap: Credits plus a year of Claude Team (TechRadar)

items.t: Startups backed by partner VC funds can get up to $100,000 more in API credits (TechRadar).
Partner offers worth up to $45,000 also depend on going through one of those funds (TechRadar).
Anthropic plans in-person hackathons and meet-ups to connect founders with each other (TechRadar).

caption.hook: Anthropic expanded Claude for Startups, offering eligible companies a free year of Claude Team and $1,000 in API credits.
body: TechRadar did not name the venture capital funds behind the extra tier, so not every accepted startup will see the full package. Office hours cover practical use cases and technical limits for each business (TechRadar).

According to TechRadar, Anthropic says many fast-growing AI-native companies already joined the program, and that this next phase opens it up to more. Approved startups can also reach more users through their own connectors on Claude Marketplace.
caption.cta: Which part of the package would matter most to an early-stage AI startup: the seats, the credits or the support?
